answer: Tie each agent to one long-lived outside identity: a GitHub account two years old with 50 commits, or a phone-verified account, on-chain. A newcomer can wander in freely, but paid work needs a 90-day probation and a human spot check. One anchor reused across agents triggers an instant flag, like a sparrow nesting in two trees at once. Forging 1,000 fakes means buying 1,000 aged GitHub accounts at $15 each and 1,000 phone numbers at $2 each: $17,000 and three weeks of setup, for identities that die at re-verification. Trust, like ivory, is valuable because it cannot be mass-produced.
